items.title: Mystical but not challenging experiences predict symptom improvement after psilocybin for treatment-resistant OCD.

summaries.en:
What if the key to breaking free from obsessive thoughts lies in a profound sense of awe and connection? New research on psilocybin for treatment-resistant OCD suggests that people who experience deep mystical states during their sessions—feelings of unity, transcendence, and timelessness—show the most lasting improvement in their symptoms, even a year later. Importantly, having a challenging or difficult trip didn't predict worse outcomes, suggesting that comfort during the experience matters less than the depth of meaning people find.

Scientists followed 27 people with OCD that hadn't responded to standard treatments, tracking their mystical experiences and OCD symptoms over a year. The findings add another piece to an exciting puzzle: across depression, anxiety, addiction, and now OCD, the same pattern keeps emerging—the most transformative therapeutic effects seem tied to these profound, awe-filled moments. This shifts how we think about healing with psychedelics: it's not just about the drug itself, but about what happens in the mind when people encounter something genuinely bigger than themselves.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis nøglen til at bryde fri fra tvangstanker ligger i en dyb følelse af undren og sammenhæng? Ny forskning om psilocybin til behandlingsresistent OCD tyder på, at mennesker, som oplever dybe mystiske tilstande under deres sessions—fornemmelser af enhed, transcendens og tidløshed—viser den mest varig forbedring af deres symptomer, selv et år senere. Det vigtige er, at en vanskelig eller ubehagelig oplevelse under sessionerne ikke forudsagde dårligere resultater, hvilket tyder på, at komforten under oplevelsen betyder mindre end den dybde af betydning, som mennesker finder.

Forskerne fulgte 27 mennesker med OCD, som ikke havde reageret på standardbehandlinger, og fulgte deres mystiske oplevelser og OCD-symptomer over et år. Resultaterne tilføjer et nyt stykke til et spændende puslespil: på tværs af depression, angst, misbrug og nu OCD ser man samme mønster igen og igen—de mest transformative terapeutiske effekter ser ud til at være forbundet med disse dybe, underfyldte øjeblikke. Dette skifter hvordan vi tænker på helbredelse med psykedelika: det handler ikke bare om stoffet selv, men om hvad der sker i sindet, når mennesker møder noget, der er virkelig større end dem selv.

items.title: A Multi-Site Evaluation of a Psychedelic Medicine Curriculum for Psychiatry Trainees.

summaries.en: Future psychiatrists are getting their first real education in psychedelic medicine—and it's making a real difference. A new 6-hour course rolled out across four U.S. psychiatry programs showed that trainees walked away with significantly better knowledge and, more importantly, genuine confidence in talking to patients about psychedelics. They felt better equipped to explain the science, discuss harm reduction, and address risks. Most had barely learned anything about psychedelics before taking the course, which tells you something about how new this field still is in medical training. This curriculum study matters because it shows we can actually teach clinicians to engage thoughtfully with this emerging medicine. As psychedelic research accelerates from labs into real clinical practice, we need doctors who understand the science and can have honest conversations with patients. This is what that pipeline looks like taking shape.
summaries.da: Fremtidens psykiatere får endelig ordentlig undervisning i psykedelika-medicin—og det gør en virkelig forskel. Et nyt 6-timers kursus på tværs af fire amerikanske psykiatri-uddannelser viste, at læger gik derfra med markant bedre viden og, vigtigere endnu, reel selvtillid til at tale med patienter om psykedelika. De følte sig bedre rustet til at forklare videnskaben, diskutere skadesreduktion og håndtere risici. De fleste havde næsten ikke lært noget om psykedelika før kurset, hvilket siger noget om hvor nyt det stadig er i medicinsk uddannelse. Dette kursusstudium betyder noget, fordi det viser, at vi faktisk kan uddanne læger til at gribe psykedelika-medicinen ansvarligt an. Mens psykedelika-forskningen accelererer fra laboratorier ind i klinikken, har vi brug for læger, der forstår videnskaben og kan have ærlige samtaler med patienter. Det er sådan denne pipeline tager form.

items.title: Feasibility and tolerability of virtual reality during esketamine treatment: A pilot study.

summaries.en: When people get ketamine treatment for depression, the experience can feel intense and uncomfortable—especially visually and aurally. Now researchers are asking: what if we could shape that experience with virtual reality? A new pilot study found that most patients were open to the idea, though early tests revealed some practical challenges (like nausea for glasses-wearers). This matters because how patients *feel* during psychedelic-assisted therapy might actually influence how well it works. As ketamine and esketamine become mainstream depression treatments, scientists are exploring whether immersive environments could make the experience safer, more tolerable, and ultimately more therapeutic.
summaries.da: Når mennesker får ketamin-behandling for depression, kan oplevelsen føles intens og ubehagelig—især visuelt og auditivt. Nu spørger forskere: hvad hvis vi kunne forme den oplevelse med virtual reality? Et nyt pilotprojekt viste, at de fleste patienter var åbne over for ideen, selvom tidlige test afslørede nogle praktiske udfordringer (som kvalme for brille-brugere). Det betyder noget, fordi hvordan patienter *føler sig* under psykedelika-assisteret terapi måske faktisk påvirker, hvor godt det virker. Efterhånden som ketamin og esketamin bliver mainstream-behandlinger for depression, udforsker videnskabsmænd, om immersive miljøer kunne gøre oplevelsen mere sikker, mere tolerabel og i sidste ende mere terapeutisk.

items.title: Real-World Therapeutic Use of Ketamine in Clinical and Non-Clinical Settings: A Cross-Sectional Survey.

summaries.en:
People self-medicating with ketamine outside clinics report similar mood improvements to those getting it under medical supervision—but here's the catch: they're also experiencing way more hallucinations and side effects, often without professional support to help them navigate it. A new study comparing real-world ketamine use across clinical and non-clinical settings reveals this stark divide, showing that while the drug's antidepressant potential is real, the setting and supervision matter enormously for safety.

Researchers used data from the 2023 Global Psychedelic Survey to map out who's using ketamine, how they're doing it, and what's actually happening. As ketamine gains attention as a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression, this research highlights a critical insight: the difference between therapeutic benefit and risky self-experimentation often comes down to having trained eyes watching your back. It's a reminder that with psychedelics, context isn't just nice to have—it's medicine.
summaries.da:
Folk der selv medicinerer med ketamin uden for klinikker rapporterer lignende stemningsforbedringer som dem, der får det under medicinske behandling—men her er hagen: de oplever langt flere hallucinationer og bivirkninger, ofte uden professionel støtte til at navigere det. Et nyt studie, der sammenligner ketaminbrug på tværs af kliniske og ikke-kliniske settings, afslører denne markante forskel og viser, at selvom stoffets antidepressiv potentiale er reelt, betyder omgivelserne og tilsynet enormt for sikkerheden.

Forskere brugte data fra den globale psykedelika-survey fra 2023 til at kortlægge, hvem der bruger ketamin, hvordan de gør det, og hvad der faktisk sker. Mens ketamin får stigende opmærksomhed som et potentielt gennembrud for behandlingsresistent depression, viser denne forskning en kritisk indsigt: forskellen mellem terapeutisk nytte og risikabel selveksperimentering handler ofte om at have trænet øjne, der passer på dig. Det er en påmindelse om, at med psykedelika er konteksten ikke bare rart at have—det er medicin.

items.title: A Multi-Site Evaluation of a Psychedelic Medicine Curriculum for Psychiatry Trainees

summaries.en: The next generation of psychiatrists is learning about psychedelics in medical school—and it's changing how they think about mental health treatment. A new study across multiple training programs shows that teaching psychiatry residents about psychedelic medicine isn't just possible, it's reshaping their understanding of what therapy can do. This matters because for decades, these conversations barely happened in clinical training. The research mapped out how different institutions are building psychedelic curricula, revealing what actually works when you're teaching future doctors about these emerging treatments. As psychedelics move from underground research into legitimate medical practice, having psychiatrists who understand the science from day one could transform how mental health care develops over the next decade.
summaries.da: Den næste generation af psykiatere lærer om psykedelika på medicinstudiet—og det ændrer på deres syn på psykisk sundhedsbehandling. Et nyt studie på tværs af flere uddannelsessteder viser, at det ikke kun er muligt at undervise psykiatrilæger om psykedelisk medicin, det omformer deres forståelse af hvad terapi kan udrette. Det betyder noget, fordi disse samtaler næsten ikke har fundet sted i klinisk uddannelse gennem årtier. Forskningen kortlagde, hvordan forskellige institutioner opbygger psykedelika-læreplaner, og afslørede hvad der virker, når man skal undervise kommende læger om disse nye behandlinger. Når psykedelika bevæger sig fra underjordisk forskning ind i legitim medicinsk praksis, kunne psykiatere, der forstår videnskaben fra dag ét, transformere hvordan psykisk sundhedsvæsen udvikler sig det kommende årti.

items.title: N,N-Dimethyltryptamine and harmine formulation alters transient EEG topography sequences near the peak of the psychedelic state

summaries.en: Your brain on psychedelics might be like a jazz musician hitting more notes, faster, and in more interesting combinations. New research on DMT and harmine—the active compounds in ayahuasca—shows that at the peak of the experience, the brain's electrical activity becomes more complex and switches between states more rapidly, yet in surprisingly predictable patterns. Scientists used EEG to track these neural state changes in 25 people across three conditions: a DMT/harmine combo, harmine alone, and placebo. The findings align with a leading theory: psychedelics don't just make your brain more chaotic—they make it more flexible and dynamic, capable of accessing a richer range of mental states. This adds another piece to the puzzle of how these compounds reshape consciousness and could eventually help us understand why they show promise in treating depression and other conditions.
summaries.da: Dit hjerne på psykedelika virker måske som en jazzmusiker, der spiller flere toner, hurtigere og i mere interessante kombinationer. Ny forskning om DMT og harmin—de aktive stoffer i ayahuasca—viser, at på toppen af oplevelsen bliver hjernens elektriske aktivitet mere kompleks og skifter mellem tilstande hurtigere, dog i overraskende forudsigelige mønstre. Forskerne brugte EEG til at spore disse neurologiske tilstandsskift hos 25 personer under tre forhold: en DMT/harmin-kombination, harmin alene og placebo. Fundet stemmer overens med en førende teori: psykedelika gør ikke bare din hjerne mere kaotisk—de gør den mere fleksibel og dynamisk, i stand til at få adgang til en mere rig vifte af mentale tilstande. Det tilføjer endnu et stykke puslespil til, hvordan disse stoffer omformer bevidstheden, og kan eventuelt hjælpe os med at forstå, hvorfor de viser lovende resultater ved behandling af depression og andre tilstande.

items.title: Layer-resolved cortical signatures of self-dissolution across psychedelics and meditation

summaries.en: What happens in your brain when the sense of 'you' dissolves? Researchers have found that psychedelics and deep meditation create remarkably similar patterns of self-dissolution—but they're now mapping exactly which layers of the brain are involved. This isn't just interesting neuroscience; it suggests these experiences tap into something fundamental about how consciousness works, and that vastly different paths (a meditation cushion or a psychedelic journey) can lead to strikingly similar states. By studying the brain's layered architecture during these profound shifts, scientists are uncovering how self-awareness is constructed—and what happens when it temporarily steps aside. This research fits into a bigger picture: we're moving beyond just asking 'do psychedelics work?' toward understanding the actual machinery behind transformation.
summaries.da: Hvad sker der i din hjerne, når fornemmelsen af 'dig selv' opløses? Forskere har opdaget, at psykedelika og dyb meditation skaber bemærkelsesværdigt ens mønstre for selvopløsning—men de kortlægger nu præcis hvilke lag af hjernen, der er involveret. Det er ikke bare interessant neuroscience; det tyder på, at disse erfaringer trykker på noget grundlæggende omkring hvordan bevidsthed fungerer, og at helt forskellige veje (en meditationspude eller en psykedelisk rejse) kan føre til slående lignende tilstande. Ved at studere hjernens lagdelte arkitektur under disse profunde skift afdækker videnskabsmænd hvordan selvbevidsthed konstrueres—og hvad der sker, når den midlertidigt træder til side. Denne forskning passer ind i et større billede: vi bevæger os ud over blot at spørge 'virker psykedelika?' mod at forstå det faktiske maskineri bag transformation.

items.title: Reply to 'Methodological concerns and interpretative limitations of assessing subjective effects of ketamine'.

summaries.en: What makes ketamine and psilocybin actually feel different to people — and does that matter for healing? New research digs into this puzzle, comparing what patients experience on these two psychedelics and how those experiences connect to real therapeutic breakthroughs. The findings suggest the subjective journey matters, but here's the catch: different studies measure these inner experiences in wildly different ways, making it hard to draw firm conclusions. Scientists are now pushing for standardized tools to capture what people actually go through — because understanding the full picture of psychedelic experience, not just symptom reduction, could unlock better treatments. This is where psychedelic science is heading: treating the whole person, not just targeting one symptom.
summaries.da: Hvad får ketamin og psilocybin egentlig til at føles forskelligt for mennesker — og betyder det noget for helbredelsen? Ny forskning dykker ned i dette puslespil, sammenlignes det folk oplever på disse to psykedelika og hvordan disse oplevelser hænger sammen med virkelig terapeutiske gennembrud. Resultaterne tyder på, at den subjektive rejse betyder noget, men her er snaghaken: forskellige studier måler disse indre oplevelser på helt forskellige måder, hvilket gør det svært at drage sikre konklusioner. Forskere presser nu på for standardiserede værktøjer til at fange det mennesker faktisk går igennem — fordi at forstå hele billedet af psykedelika-oplevelsen, ikke kun symptomreduktion, kunne låse op for bedre behandlinger. Det er her psykedelika-forskningen er på vej hen: at behandle hele mennesket, ikke bare målrette ét symptom.

items.title: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice

summaries.en: Here's something surprising: in a new study, psilocybin and a similar psychedelic actually *increased* how strongly mice remembered scary experiences—the opposite of what researchers expected. Scientists gave stressed mice a single dose and found the effect stuck around for days. This might sound backwards, but it could be revealing something crucial: psychedelics might work by helping us process emotional memories differently, not by making us forget them. The research used mice exposed to chronic stress, then measured their fear responses after the psychedelic dose. As psychedelic science accelerates toward real-world therapies for anxiety and trauma, understanding exactly how these compounds reshape our emotional brains—even when results surprise us—is essential. These animal studies are the foundation for figuring out whether psychedelics can help people break free from overwhelming fear and worry.
summaries.da: Her kommer noget overraskende: i et nyt studie fik psilocybin og et lignende psykedelikum faktisk mus til at *huske* skræmmende oplevelser *stærkere*—det modsatte af hvad forskerne forventede. Videnskabsmænd gav stressede mus en enkelt dosis og fandt ud af, at effekten holdt i flere dage. Det kan lyde bagvendt, men det kunne afsløre noget afgørende: psykedelika virker måske ved at hjælpe os til at behandle følelsesminder anderledes, ikke ved at lade os glemme dem. Forskningen brugte mus udsat for kronisk stress og målte deres frygtrespons efter psykedelika-dosen. Mens psykedelika-forskningen accelererer mod virkelige terapi for angst og traume, er det afgørende at forstå præcis, hvordan disse stoffer omformer vores følelsesmæssige hjerner—selv når resultaterne overrasker os. Disse dyrestudier er fundamentet for at finde ud af, om psykedelika kan hjælpe mennesker til at bryde fri fra overvældende frygt og bekymring.

items.title: N,N-Dimethyltryptamine and harmine formulation alters transient EEG topography sequences near the peak of the psychedelic state.

summaries.en: Your brain during a psychedelic trip is busier and more complex than we thought. When researchers gave people a combination of DMT and harmine (ingredients from ayahuasca), their brain waves showed something unexpected: neural states were switching faster, following more intricate patterns, yet paradoxically becoming more predictable. It's like your brain was conducting a more elaborate symphony with stricter rules. This double-blind EEG study tracked how these two molecules reshaped the brain's electrical activity at the peak of the experience, revealing that psychedelics don't just make neural signals more random—they reorganise how different brain states connect and flow into one another. As researchers hunt for why psychedelics might help with depression and trauma, this finding matters: understanding the brain's choreography during these states brings us closer to understanding how they might catalyse genuine change.
summaries.da: Dit hjerne under en psykedelisk oplevelse er mere aktiv og kompleks, end vi troede. Da forskere gav mennesker en blanding af DMT og harmin (ingredienser fra ayahuasca), viste deres hjernebølger noget uventet: neural tilstande skiftede hurtigere, fulgte mere intrikate mønstre, men blev samtidig mere forudsigelige. Det er som om dit hjerne dirigerede en mere raffineret symfoni efter strengere regler. Dette dobbeltblindt EEG-studie fulgte, hvordan disse to molekyler omstrukturerede hjernens elektriske aktivitet på oplevelsens højdepunkt, og viste at psykedelika ikke blot gør neural signalering mere tilfældig—de reorganiserer, hvordan forskellige hjernestilstande forbinder og flyder ind i hinanden. Mens forskere jagter svaret på, hvorfor psykedelika kan hjælpe med depression og trauma, betyder denne opdagelse noget: at forstå hjernens koreografi i disse tilstande bringer os tættere på at forstå, hvordan de kan katalysere ægte forandring.

items.title: Modulation of GABA and glutamate by ketamine in depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis of magnetic resonance spectroscopy studies.

summaries.en:
Ketamine is famous for lifting depression fast, but exactly how it rewires the brain's chemistry has remained fuzzy. A new analysis of brain-imaging studies tried to crack this puzzle by looking at how ketamine changes two key brain chemicals—GABA and glutamate—that are often out of balance in depression. The surprise? The studies didn't find consistent changes, which tells us we're still missing pieces of the story.

Researchers combed through over 1,000 studies and carefully analysed 11 rigorous ones, but found huge differences in how they measured things—different brain regions, different timings, different methods. This scattered picture means we need smarter, more standardised studies to understand how psychedelics like ketamine actually restore balance in the depressed brain. The good news: this research is happening, and each puzzle piece gets us closer to designing even better treatments.
summaries.da:
Ketamin er berømt for at løfte depression hurtigt, men præcis hvordan det omstrukturerer hjernens kemi, er forblevet uklart. En ny analyse af hjernebillede-studier forsøgte at løse dette puslespil ved at se på, hvordan ketamin ændrer to nøglekemikalier i hjernen—GABA og glutamat—som ofte er ude af balance ved depression. Overraskelsen? Studierne fandt ikke konsistente ændringer, hvilket fortæller os, at vi stadig mangler brikker af historien.

Forskere gennemgik over 1.000 studier og analyserede grundigt 11 grundige, men fandt enorme forskelle i hvordan de målte tingene—forskellige hjernebygninger, forskellige timinger, forskellige metoder. Dette spredte billede betyder, at vi har brug for smartere, mere standardiserede studier for at forstå, hvordan psykedelika som ketamin faktisk genopretter balancen i den deprimerede hjerne. Det gode nyt: denne forskning foregår, og hver puslespilsbrik bringer os tættere på at designe endnu bedre behandlinger.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of a modified-release psilocybin formulation: A SAD Phase I trial in normal-weight and overweight/obese participants.

summaries.en: Scientists just tested a new way to give psilocybin—a slow-release pill that keeps levels steady in your body instead of spiking fast. The good news? It was safe and well-tolerated across the board, with no serious side effects, even in people living with obesity. This matters because it opens the door to using psychedelics at doses so subtle you wouldn't actually "trip," but your brain chemistry might still benefit. Researchers gave healthy adults escalating doses (0.5 to 2 mg) in this controlled Phase I trial, measuring exactly how the compound moved through their bodies. What they found fits into a bigger shift in psychedelic science: moving beyond the dramatic therapeutic experience toward precise, personalized medicine. This slow-release approach could be key for treating metabolic issues like obesity, where steady serotonin modulation might help without requiring intense psychological intervention. The field is maturing—from countercultural curiosity to pharmaceutical precision.
summaries.da: Forskere har netop testet en ny måde at give psilocybin på—en depotformulering, der holder niveauerne stabile i kroppen i stedet for at skyde i vejret hurtigt. Det gode? Det var sikkert og godt tolereret på tværs af gruppen, uden alvorlige bivirkninger, selv hos mennesker med fedme. Det betyder noget, fordi det åbner døren til at bruge psykedelika i doser så subtile, at du ikke ville "trippe", men din hjernekemi kunne stadig få gavn. Forskerne gav raske voksne stigende doser (0,5 til 2 mg) i dette kontrollerede fase I-forsøg og målte præcist, hvordan stoffet bevægede sig gennem kroppen. Det, de fandt, passer ind i et større skift inden for psykedelikaforskning: bevægelse væk fra den dramatiske terapeutiske oplevelse mod præcis, personaliseret medicin. Denne depotformulering kunne være nøglen til at behandle metaboliske problemer som fedme, hvor stabil serotoninmodulering kunne hjælpe uden intens psykologisk intervention. Feltet modnes—fra kontrakulturel nysgerrighed til farmaceutisk præcision.

items.title: An Open-Label, Dose-Escalation Trial of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for Bipolar II Depression.

summaries.en:
What if a single dose of psilocybin could lift depression that hasn't budged with standard treatment? A new trial is exploring exactly that—giving psilocybin-assisted therapy to people with bipolar II depression, carefully increasing doses to find what actually works. Early findings suggest something genuinely promising is happening, offering real hope for the roughly one-third of people whose depression resists conventional medications.

Researchers conducted an open-label dose-escalation study, meaning participants knew they were receiving psilocybin and doses were increased gradually based on safety and response. This work fits into a broader shift in psychiatry: psychedelics are moving from underground whispers to legitimate clinical research, with serious institutions now investigating their potential for treatment-resistant mood disorders. It's a reminder that sometimes the most transformative breakthroughs come from directions medicine had written off.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis en enkelt dosis psilocybin kunne løfte depression, som almindelig behandling ikke rører? Et nyt forsøg udforsker netop det—at give psilocybin-assisteret terapi til mennesker med bipolar II depression, idet man forsigtigt øger doserne for at finde, hvad der virker. Tidlige fund tyder på, at noget virkelig lovende er på gang, og giver håb til omkring en tredjedel af mennesker, hvis depression modstår almindelige lægemidler.

Forskere gennemførte et åbent dosis-eskaleringsforsøg, hvilket betyder at deltagerne vidste, de fik psilocybin, og doserne blev gradvist øget baseret på sikkerhed og respons. Dette arbejde passer ind i en bredere ændring inden for psykiatri: psykedelika bevæger sig fra underjordiske hvislen til legitim klinisk forskning, hvor seriøse institutioner nu udforsker deres potentiale for behandlingsresistent humørlidelser. Det er en påmindelse om, at nogle gange kommer de mest transformative gennembrud fra retninger, medicinen havde skrevet af.

items.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Single-Ascending-Dose Study to Identify a Subperceptual Dose of Psilocybin in Healthy Adults

summaries.en:
What if psilocybin could help treat depression and anxiety without the intense trip? New research suggests it might be possible. Scientists gave healthy adults tiny doses of psilocybin—ranging from half a milligram to four milligrams—and found that at the lowest doses, people experienced barely any hallucinations or altered thinking, yet their brains still showed clear signs of activity. This opens a fascinating possibility: the therapeutic benefits might exist at doses so subtle that people wouldn't need to spend hours in a clinic room watching the walls breathe.

In this carefully controlled Phase 1 study, researchers escalated doses step-by-step while monitoring safety, and found no serious side effects—just occasional drowsiness, comparable to placebo. The real breakthrough is understanding where the "perceptual threshold" actually sits: subjective effects only became noticeable around 2.5 mg, while brain changes (measured through pupil response) started appearing at even lower doses. As psychedelic medicine moves toward real-world clinical use, this kind of foundational mapping is crucial—it helps researchers figure out whether we're chasing the experience itself or something deeper in how these molecules rewire struggling minds.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis psykedelika kunne behandle depression og angst uden det intense trip? Nyforskning tyder på, at det kunne være muligt. Forskere gav sunde voksne mikroskopiske doser psilocybin—fra et halvt til fire milligram—og fandt ud af, at ved de laveste doser oplevede mennesker næsten ingen hallucinationer eller ændret tænkning, alligevel viste deres hjerner klare tegn på aktivitet. Det åbner en fascinerende mulighed: de terapeutiske fordele kunne eksistere ved doser så subtile, at mennesker ikke skulle bruge timer på en klinisk stue og se væggene pulsere.

I dette omhyggeligt kontrollerede Phase 1-studie øgede forskerne doserne trin for trin, mens de overvågede sikkerhed, og fandt ingen alvorlige bivirkninger—bare lejlighedsvis søvnighed, som hos placebo. Det rigtige gennembrud er at forstå, hvor "perceptionstærsklen" ligger: subjektive effekter blev først mærkbare omkring 2,5 mg, mens hjernens ændringer (målt gennem pupilreaktion) startede ved endnu lavere doser. Når psykedelisk medicin bevæger sig mod klinisk brug i den virkelige verden, er denne slags grundlæggende kortlægning afgørende—det hjælper forskere med at finde ud af, om vi jagter oplevelsen selv eller noget dybere i, hvordan disse molekyler omformer besværede sind.

items.title: A circuit dissection of perception-action decoupling in S-ketamine-induced hallucination-like states.

summaries.en: Researchers using ketamine in mice have discovered something fascinating: the brain's ability to perceive threats and the ability to act on those perceptions can become dangerously disconnected. Under ketamine's influence, mice "heard" threats that weren't there and their behavior fell apart—but not because they couldn't hear properly. Instead, two specific brain pathways got hijacked. One pathway, connecting the amygdala to the striatum, started seeing danger everywhere. The other, from the prefrontal cortex, lost its ability to organize coherent behavior. Using advanced imaging and circuit manipulation, scientists pinpointed exactly how ketamine scrambles these signals, shifting brain activity into a chaotic, poorly-coordinated state. This matters because hallucinations in psychiatric conditions likely involve similar breakdowns—and now we know where to look. Understanding how these pathways normally keep perception and action in sync opens new doors for treating disorders where they fall apart.
summaries.da: Forskere har gjort en fascinerende opdagelse ved hjælp af ketamin på mus: hjernens evne til at opfatte trusler og evnen til at handle på disse opfattelser kan blive farligt afkoblet. Under ketamins påvirkning "hørte" mus trusler, der slet ikke var der, og deres adfærd blev kaotisk—men ikke fordi de ikke kunne høre ordentligt. I stedet blev to specifikke hjernebaner kidnappet. Den ene bane, fra amygdala til striatum, begyndte at se fare overalt. Den anden, fra præfrontal cortex, mistede evnen til at organisere sammenhængende adfærd. Ved hjælp af avanceret billeddannelse og kredsløbsmanipulation identificerede forskerne præcist, hvordan ketamin roer disse signaler, og skifter hjernens aktivitet til en kaotisk, dårligt koordineret tilstand. Det betyder noget, fordi hallucinationer ved psykiatriske lidelser sandsynligvis involverer lignende sammenbrud—og nu ved vi, hvor vi skal kigge. At forstå, hvordan disse baner normalt holder opfattelse og handling i sync, åbner nye døre for behandling af tilstande, hvor de falder fra hinanden.

items.title: Cognitive effects of ketamine and esketamine treatment for major depressive and bipolar disorder: a systematic review.

summaries.en: Depression and bipolar disorder don't just affect mood—they fog up thinking, memory, and focus. Here's what's interesting: while most antidepressants leave cognition untouched, ketamine and esketamine show promise in actually sharpening mental clarity. A new review of 22 studies found that people receiving these treatments experienced improvements in memory, attention, and processing speed—the stuff that makes daily life feel manageable again. The catch? Single doses show mixed results, but ongoing ketamine treatment appears more consistently beneficial. This matters because depression steals cognitive function, and most treatments don't give it back. As psychedelics reshape psychiatry, research like this reveals they might not just lift mood—they could restore the mental sharpness people desperately need to rebuild their lives.
summaries.da: Depression og bipolær disorder påvirker ikke kun humøret—de tåger også tankeevne, hukommelse og koncentration. Her er det interessante: mens de fleste antidepressiver lader kognition uberørt, viser ketamin og esketamin potentiale til faktisk at skærpe mental klarhed. En ny gennemgang af 22 studier viser, at mennesker under behandling oplevede forbedringer i hukommelse, opmærksomhed og bearbejdelseshastighed—det som gør dagligdagen håndterbar. Fangsten? Enkeltdoser viser blandede resultater, men løbende ketaminbehandling virker mere konsistent gavnlig. Det betyder noget, fordi depression stjæler kognitiv funktion, og de fleste behandlinger giver den ikke tilbage. Efterhånden som psykedelika omformer psykiatrien, viser forskning som denne, at de måske ikke blot løfter humøret—de kunne genoprette den mentale skarphed, som mennesker desperat har brug for.

items.title: Psychedelics and suicidality: A double-edged sword - risks, mechanisms, and moving forward.

summaries.en: Psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD are showing real promise for treating depression and other mental health conditions tied to suicidal thoughts—but a new review reveals a complicated truth: the same mechanisms that help people heal can sometimes trigger crises in vulnerable individuals or without proper support. Researchers analysed rare reports of increased suicidality linked to psychedelic use, finding that while deaths have occurred in unsafe recreational settings, serious problems in clinical trials remain uncommon and no clearer than with placebo. The key insight? Psychedelics reduce fear of death and change how we see the world—powerful shifts that can liberate people from suffering, but also destabilise those without adequate care. As psychedelic research accelerates, this study maps the territory we need to navigate carefully: not abandoning these tools, but understanding exactly how to use them safely.
summaries.da: Psykedelika som psilocybin og LSD viser lovende resultater til behandling af depression og andre psykiske tilstande forbundet med selvmordstanker—men en ny analyse afslører en kompleks sandhed: de samme mekanismer, der hjælper mennesker med at hele, kan nogle gange udløse kriser hos sårbare personer eller uden ordentlig støtte. Forskere analyserede sjældne rapporter om øget selvmordsfaren knyttet til psykedelika-brug og fandt, at mens dødsfald er sket i usikre rekreative sammenhænge, forbliver alvorlige problemer i kliniske forsøg ualmindelige og ikke tydeligt værre end placebo. Nøgleindsigten? Psykedelika reducerer dødsangst og ændrer hvordan vi ser verden—kraftfulde skift, der kan befri mennesker fra lidelse, men også destabilisere dem uden tilstrækkelig omsorg. Når psykedelika-forskningen accelererer, kortlægger denne undersøgelse territoriet, vi skal navigere omhyggeligt: ikke ved at opgive disse værktøjer, men ved at forstå præcist hvordan man bruger dem sikkert.

items.title: A national approach in a European context: Multidisciplinary and multiprofessional recommendations on the clinical use of psychedelic substances.

summaries.en: Psychedelics like psilocybin and MDMA are showing real promise for treating depression, PTSD, and other mental health conditions — but getting them safely into clinics requires serious groundwork. Portugal just did something remarkable: pharmacists, psychologists, and doctors joined forces with ethics boards to create the first unified national framework for psychedelic therapy, covering everything from informed consent to training requirements. This isn't just about one country — it's a blueprint showing how Europe can move psychedelic research from the lab into actual clinical practice responsibly. As more studies prove these treatments work, we're at a crucial moment where good guidelines separate genuine medicine from chaos.
summaries.da: Psykedelika som psilocybin og MDMA viser real lovende resultater for depression, PTSD og andre psykiske lidelser — men at få dem sikkert ud i klinikkerne kræver seriøst forberedelsesarbejde. Portugal gjorde netop noget bemærkelsesværdigt: farmaceuter, psykologer og læger gik sammen med etikråd for at skabe Europas første enhedlige nationale rammeværk for psykedelika-terapi, der dækker alt fra informeret samtykke til træningskrav. Det er ikke bare om ét land — det er en skabelon, der viser, hvordan Europa kan flytte psykedelika-forskningen fra laboratoriet ind i faktisk klinisk praksis på ansvarlig vis. Efterhånden som flere studier beviser, at disse behandlinger virker, står vi på et afgørende tidspunkt, hvor gode retningslinjer adskiller ægte medicin fra kaos.

items.title: Psychedelics and suicidality: A double-edged sword - risks, mechanisms, and moving forward

summaries.en: Psychedelics like LSD and psilocybin are showing real promise for treating depression and trauma—but here's what scientists are wrestling with: in rare cases, they might increase suicidal thoughts, especially in people without proper support. A new study maps out why this double-edge sword exists: the same shifts in how you see the world and fear that can heal deep wounds might, for some vulnerable people, create crisis instead. Researchers reviewed data from both recreational and clinical settings, finding that while serious problems are uncommon and don't differ from placebo in trials, the risks are real enough to take seriously. This isn't a reason to stop psychedelic research—it's actually pushing the field toward better screening, safer settings, and smarter ways to identify who needs extra care. As psychedelics move from lab to clinic, understanding these risks is becoming just as important as understanding their potential.
summaries.da: Psykedelika som LSD og psilocybin viser lovende resultater mod depression og traumer—men her er det, videnskabsfolk kæmper med: i sjældne tilfælde kan de øge selvmordstanker, særligt hos mennesker uden ordentlig støtte. Et nyt studie kortlægger hvorfor denne dobbeltsidet sværd findes: de samme skift i hvordan du ser verden og frygt, der kan hele dybe sår, kan måske skabe krise hos nogle sårbare mennesker. Forskere gennemgik data fra både fritids- og kliniske indstillinger og fandt, at mens alvorlige problemer er sjældne og ikke adskiller sig fra placebo i studier, er risiciene reelle nok til at tage alvorligt. Dette er ikke en grund til at stoppe psykedelika-forskning—det presser faktisk området mod bedre screening, sikrere miljøer og smartere måder at identificere hvem der har brug for ekstra omsorg. Når psykedelika bevæger sig fra lab til klinik, bliver forståelse af disse risici lige så vigtig som forståelse af deres potentiale.

items.title: Short-term ketamine interventions for depressive disorders: practical best-practice recommendations for psychiatrists using oral, subcutaneous, and nasal formulations.

summaries.en: When depression won't budge with standard antidepressants, ketamine might offer a lifeline—and it's working fast. Recent research shows that ketamine and esketamine can dramatically reduce depressive symptoms in days or weeks, not months, giving people who are really struggling a genuine shot at relief. Psychiatrists now have practical guidance on how to use different forms of ketamine—pills, injections, nasal sprays—safely and effectively. This narrative review synthesized evidence across studies and regulatory frameworks to create a roadmap for doctors. The findings fit into an exciting shift in psychiatry: we're moving beyond waiting for medication to slowly kick in. Psychedelics and ketamine are opening doors to faster, more targeted interventions for the hardest-to-treat cases, and understanding how to use these tools properly is crucial as they become more available.
summaries.da: Når depression ikke giver efter for almindelige antidepressiva, kan ketamin tilbyde håb—og det virker hurtigt. Ny forskning viser, at ketamin og esketamin kan mindske depressive symptomer dramatisk inden for dage eller uger, ikke måneder, og giver mennesker, der virkelig kæmper, en reel chance for lindring. Psykiatere har nu praktisk vejledning i, hvordan man bruger forskellige former for ketamin—piller, injektioner, næsespray—sikkert og effektivt. Denne forskningsgennemgang sammensyntesiserede beviser på tværs af studier og reguleringsrammer for at skabe et kort for læger. Fundet passer ind i en spændende udvikling inden for psykiatri: vi bevæger os væk fra at vente på, at medicin langsomt virker. Psykedelika og ketamin åbner døre til hurtigere, mere målrettede behandlinger for de vanskeligste tilfælde, og at forstå, hvordan man bruger disse værktøjer korrekt, er afgørende, mens de bliver mere tilgængelige.

items.title: An Open-Label, Dose-Escalation Trial of Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for Bipolar II Depression

summaries.en: What if psilocybin could help people with bipolar II depression find relief when traditional treatments fall short? A new trial is exploring exactly that—giving carefully dosed psilocybin alongside therapy to people living with this notoriously difficult form of depression. Early results suggest this combination might offer genuine hope for those who've struggled to find answers. Researchers gradually increased doses in a controlled setting, watching closely to understand both benefits and safety. This study slots into a broader shift in psychiatry: psychedelics are moving from counterculture myth to serious medicine, with growing evidence suggesting they could reshape how we treat stubborn mood disorders.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis psykedelika kunne hjælpe mennesker med bipolar II depression, når traditionelle behandlinger ikke virker? Et nyt forsøg udforsker netop det—at give omhyggeligt doseret psilocybin sammen med terapi til mennesker, der lever med denne notorisk svære depressionsform. Tidlige resultater tyder på, at denne kombination kan give reel håb for dem, der har kæmpet for at finde svar. Forskere øgede gradvist doserne i kontrollererede forhold og overvågede nøje både fordele og sikkerhed. Dette studie passer ind i en bredere udvikling inden for psykiatri: psykedelika bevæger sig fra modekultmyte til seriøs medicin, med voksende evidens for, at de kunne omforme hvordan vi behandler hårdnakkede stemningsforstyrrelser.

items.title: Serotonergic psychedelics and amphetamine shift male rat ultrasonic vocalizations toward call patterns associated with positively valenced states.

summaries.en:
Rats on psychedelics and amphetamine literally sound happier. Researchers used AI to analyze nearly 48,000 ultrasonic calls from rats given LSD, DOI, or amphetamine, finding that these substances shifted their "vocal repertoire" away from neutral alarm calls and toward patterns linked to positive emotional states. It's a clever way to peek into what animals might be feeling—when rats are rewarded or content, their calls change in characteristic ways, and psychedelics seem to nudge them in that direction.

The study used machine learning to map rat vocalizations with precision, revealing that psychedelics don't just make rats chattier, they change *what* they're "saying." This fits into a growing picture in psychedelic research: these compounds appear to shift brain states toward more positive, engaged modes—something we see in human studies too. It's early-stage work, but it adds another piece of evidence that psychedelics genuinely alter emotional and neural states in measurable ways.
summaries.da:
Rotter på psykedelika og amfetamin lyder bogstaveligt talt gladere. Forskere brugte kunstig intelligens til at analysere næsten 48.000 ultralydskald fra rotter, der blev givet LSD, DOI eller amfetamin, og fandt, at disse stoffer skiftede deres "vokalrepertoire" væk fra neutrale alarmkald og mod mønstre forbundet med positive følelsestilstande. Det er en smart måde at få indsigt i, hvad dyr måske føler—når rotter bliver belønnet eller er tilfredse, ændres deres kald på karakteristiske måder, og psykedelika ser ud til at skubbe dem i den retning.

Studiet brugte maskinlæring til at kortlægge rottekaldelyden med præcision og viste, at psykedelika ikke bare gør rotter snavsere; de ændrer *hvad* de "siger." Det passer ind i et voksende billede inden for psykedelikaforskning: disse stoffer ser ud til at skifte hjernens tilstand mod mere positive, engagerede tilstande—noget vi også ser i menneskestudier. Det er tidligt arbejde, men det tilføjer endnu et bevis på, at psykedelika virkelig ændrer følelsesmæssige og neurale tilstande på målbare måder.

items.title: Novel pharmacotherapies for opioid use disorder and opioid withdrawal.

summaries.en:
The opioid crisis isn't going away—and traditional medications alone aren't enough. A new review reveals promising alternatives on the horizon: ketamine shows early signs of reducing cravings and withdrawal symptoms, cannabidiol may ease anxiety-driven relapse, and psychedelics like ibogaine demonstrate potential for breaking the withdrawal cycle. These aren't replacements for existing treatments, but they target the brain's reward system in completely new ways, potentially helping people who haven't responded to standard care.

Scientists examined emerging therapies across multiple drug classes to understand how they could complement methadone and buprenorphine. The evidence is still early—especially for psychedelics, where safety and regulation remain thorny issues—but the pattern is clear: we're moving toward a toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. This research signals a crucial shift in how we think about addiction treatment: not just blocking opioid receptors, but actually rewiring the brain systems that drive dependence. It's a reminder that when one path isn't working, science keeps looking for new ones.
summaries.da:
Opioidkrisen forsvinder ikke—og traditionelle medicin alene er ikke nok. En ny review afslører lovende alternativer på horisonten: ketamin viser tidlige tegn på at reducere trang og abstinensymptomer, cannabidiol kan lette angst-drevet tilbagefald, og psykedelika som ibogain demonstrerer potentiale for at bryde abstinencyklussen. Det er ikke erstatninger for eksisterende behandlinger, men de målretter hjernens belønningssystem på helt nye måder og kan potentielt hjælpe mennesker, som ikke har responderet på standardbehandling.

Forskere undersøgte nye terapier på tværs af flere stofklasser for at forstå, hvordan de kunne supplere methadon og buprenorphin. Beviserne er stadig tidlige—især for psykedelika, hvor sikkerhed og regulering stadig er vanskelige spørgsmål—men mønstret er klart: vi bevæger os mod et værktøjskasse i stedet for en tilgang, der passer alle. Denne forskning signalerer et afgørende skifte i, hvordan vi tænker på afhængighedsbehandling: ikke blot at blokere opioidreceptorer, men faktisk at omvire hjernens systemer, der driver afhængighed. Det er en påmindelse om, at når en vej ikke virker, fortsætter videnskaben med at søge nye.

items.title: A Case of Acute Mania and Rhabdomyolysis Associated With Long-Term, Daily Psilocybin Use

summaries.en: A new case study is raising important questions about what happens when people use psilocybin every single day for extended periods. Researchers documented a person who developed severe manic symptoms and a dangerous muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis linked to long-term daily psilocybin use—a rare but serious finding that reminds us these substances deserve careful, honest attention. This single case report is exactly the kind of clinical observation that helps the field understand not just the potential benefits of psychedelics, but their real-world risks too. As psychedelic research expands and more people explore these substances, this kind of rigorous documentation matters: it's how we build the nuanced, balanced picture we need to use these tools safely and responsibly.
summaries.da: Et nyt case-studie stiller vigtige spørgsmål om, hvad der sker, når mennesker bruger psilocybin hver eneste dag over længere tid. Forskere dokumenterede en person, der udviklede alvorlige maniske symptomer og en farlig muskellidelse kaldet rabdomyolyse knyttet til langtidsligt daglig psilocybin-brug—et sjældent, men alvorligt fund, som minder os om, at disse stoffer fortjener opmærksom, ærlighed. Denne case-rapport er præcis den slags klinisk observation, der hjælper området med at forstå ikke blot psykedelikas potentielle fordele, men også deres faktiske risici. Som psykedelisk forskning udvides og flere mennesker udforsker disse stoffer, betyder denne form for streng dokumentation noget: det er sådan, vi opbygger det nuancerede, afbalancerede billede, vi har brug for for at bruge disse værktøjer sikkert og ansvarligt.

items.title: Psilocybin restores social novelty investigation in male SAPAP3 knockout mice and engages prefrontal-hippocampal circuitry.

summaries.en: Here's something striking: when researchers gave psilocybin to mice with a genetic condition that made them socially withdrawn and compulsive, something remarkable happened. These mice started seeking out new social interactions again—a behavior they'd lost. Even a single dose created changes that lasted at least a week. The study used standard mouse models of OCD and brain imaging to track what was happening, finding that psilocybin specifically activated two brain regions linked to social thinking: the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. What makes this exciting is that social withdrawal in OCD is often overlooked by doctors, even though it causes real suffering. Psychedelics are opening doors we didn't know existed—not just for mood or anxiety, but for helping people reconnect with others. This is the kind of precise, careful research that's building the case for psychedelics in psychiatry.
summaries.da: Her er noget slående: da forskere gav psykedelika til mus med en genetisk tilstand, der gjorde dem socialt tilbagetrukne og tvangsmæssige, skete der noget bemærkelsesværdigt. Disse mus begyndte igen at søge ny social kontakt—en adfærd de havde mistet. Selv en enkelt dosis skabte forandringer, der varede mindst en uge. Studiet brugte standardmus-modeller af OCD og hjernebilleddannelse til at spore hvad der skete, og fandt at psykedelika specifikt aktiverede to hjernereioner forbundet med social tænkning: præfrontal cortex og hippocampus. Det spændende er, at social tilbagetrækning ved OCD ofte bliver overset af læger, selvom det forårsager ægte lidelse. Psykedelika åbner døre, vi ikke vidste fandtes—ikke kun for humør eller angst, men for at hjælpe mennesker til at genforbinde med hinanden. Dette er netop den slags præcis, omhyggelig forskning, der bygger sagen for psykedelika inden for psykiatri.

items.title: Mechanistic Basis for 5-HT2AR Over 5-HT2BR Activation

summaries.en: Scientists just cracked a crucial code for safer psychedelic medicines. The challenge: psychedelics work brilliantly on one brain receptor (5-HT2A), but can cause heart valve problems by activating another (5-HT2B). Now researchers have figured out exactly how to design molecules that hit the therapeutic target while avoiding the dangerous one—like threading a molecular needle. They tested their blueprint with a new compound called IHCH-2330 and confirmed it works using cutting-edge 3D imaging. This isn't just lab success; it's the kind of precision design that could let us harness psychedelika's healing potential without the health risks that have worried regulators. We're watching real-time progress in turning psychedelics into safe, targeted medicines.
summaries.da: Forskere har netop knækket en vigtig kode for sikrere psykedelika-medicin. Udfordringen: psykedelika virker glimrende på en hjernereceptor (5-HT2A), men kan give hjerteklapproblemer ved at aktivere en anden (5-HT2B). Nu har forskere fundet ud af præcis, hvordan man designer molekyler, der rammer det terapeutiske mål uden at ramme det farlige—som at trække en molekylær nål. De testede deres design med et nyt stof kaldet IHCH-2330 og bekræftede det virker med avanceret 3D-billeddannelse. Det er ikke bare laboratoriessucces; det er præcisionsdesign, der kunne lade os udnytte psykedelikas helbredende potentiale uden de helbredsmæssige risici, som har bekymret regulatorer. Vi oplever realtidsfremskridt i at gøre psykedelika til sikker, målrettet medicin.

items.title: Psilocybin restores social novelty investigation in male SAPAP3 knockout mice and engages prefrontal–hippocampal circuitry

summaries.en: What if a psychedelic could help restore social connection in people struggling with obsessive-compulsive disorder? New research shows psilocybin reversed social withdrawal in mice with compulsive behaviors, helping them engage with new social contacts again—an effect that lasted a week after just one dose. Scientists traced this recovery to activity in specific brain regions involved in social thinking and memory, suggesting psychedelics might work by rewiring how our brains process social information. This study adds crucial evidence to a growing picture: psychedelics aren't just producing altered states, they're potentially reshaping brain circuits in ways that could address real symptoms that standard treatments often miss. As research moves toward human trials, findings like these help explain why people report feeling more socially connected after psychedelic experiences—and why scientists are increasingly excited about their therapeutic potential.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis et psykedelikum kunne hjælpe med at genoprette social kontakt hos mennesker, der kæmper med tvangslidelse? Ny forskning viser, at psilocybin vendte social tilbagetrækning hos mus med tvangspræget adfærd, hvilket hjalp dem med at engagere sig i ny social kontakt igen—en effekt, der varede en uge efter kun én dosis. Forskere sporede denne bedring til aktivitet i specifikke hjernebaner involveret i social tænkning og hukommelse, hvilket tyder på, at psykedelika virker ved at omstrukturere, hvordan vores hjerner behandler social information. Denne undersøgelse tilføjer afgørende beviser til et voksende billede: psykedelika producerer ikke bare ændrede bevidsthedstilstande, de omstrukturerer potentielt hjernebaner på måder, der kunne adressere rigtige symptomer, som standardbehandlinger ofte overser. Når forskningen bevæger sig mod menneskeforsøg, hjælper findings som disse med at forklare, hvorfor mennesker rapporterer at føle sig mere socialt forbundet efter psykedeliske oplevelser—og hvorfor forskere bliver stadig mere begejstrede for deres terapeutiske potentiale.

items.title: Structure-based design of subtype-selective psychedelic analogs

summaries.en:
Imagine a psychedelic medicine that gives you the therapeutic benefits without the cardiac risks—researchers just moved closer to making it real. Scientists have designed new psychedelic compounds that activate the brain receptor responsible for healing depression and PTSD, while deliberately avoiding a different receptor that can damage the heart. This is a game-changer because classical psychedelics trigger both, and that heart problem has been a genuine safety concern holding back their medical use.

Using cutting-edge cryo-EM imaging to map receptor structures at atomic detail, the team engineered compounds that discriminate between two nearly identical serotonin receptors—a feat many thought impossible. The new molecules worked in animal depression models and represent a blueprint for safer psychedelic medicines. This fits perfectly into psychedelic research's current momentum: we're moving from "does this work?" to "how can we make it work better and safer?" That's the sign of a field growing up.
summaries.da:
Forestil dig et psykedelika-medicin, der giver dig de terapeutiske fordele uden hjerteskaderne—forskere er netop kommet tættere på det virkelighed. Videnskabsmænd har designet nye psykedelika-forbindelser, der aktiverer hjernereceptoren bag depression og PTSD-helbredelse, samtidig med at de bevidst undgår en anden receptor, der kan skade hjertet. Det er afgørende, fordi klassiske psykedelika påvirker begge dele, og det hjerteproblem har været en ægte sikkerhedsbetænkelighed, der holder deres medicinske brug tilbage.

Med ultranmoderne cryo-EM-billeddannelse til at kortlægge receptorstrukturer på atomær detaljegrad designede holdet forbindelser, der skelner mellem to næsten identiske serotoninreceptorer—en bedrift mange troede var umulig. De nye molekyler virkede i dyrmodeller for depression og udgør en blueprint for sikrere psykedelika-medicin. Det passer perfekt til psykedelika-forskningens nuværende fremdrift: vi går fra "virker det?" til "hvordan gør vi det bedre og sikrere?" Det er tegnet på et felt, der bliver voksent.

items.title: Validating and creating a short-form of the persisting effects questionnaire: A measure of positive and negative outcomes from psychedelic experiences.

summaries.en: Here's something quietly important: researchers just figured out how to properly measure what psychedelics actually do to people over time. The old questionnaire was over 140 items long and kind of a mess—turns out it wasn't even measuring what people thought it was. The new version? 14 focused questions that clearly separate positive effects (like insight and connection) from negative ones (like anxiety or confusion). Scientists tested this with real data from both therapy sessions and research studies, making sure the questions actually make sense to people. This matters because psychedelic research is getting serious—moving from curiosity into medicine. You need solid measurement tools to understand what's really happening, spot who benefits most, and eventually help doctors know how to use these substances safely. This validated questionnaire is like getting a reliable thermometer for the field.
summaries.da: Her er noget stille vigtigt: forskere har lige fundet ud af, hvordan man skal måle hvad psykedelika rent faktisk gør ved mennesker over tid. Det gamle spørgeskema havde over 140 spørgsmål og var en rod—det viste sig, at det ikke engang målte det, som folk troede det gjorde. Den nye version? 14 fokuserede spørgsmål, som klart adskiller positive effekter (som indsigt og forbindelse) fra negative (som angst eller forvirring). Forskerne testede det med rigtige data fra både terapisessioner og forskningsstudier og sikrede sig, at spørgsmålene giver mening for mennesker. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelikaforskning bliver seriøs—bevæger sig fra nysgerrighed ind i medicin. Du skal bruge pålidelige målingsværktøjer til at forstå hvad der virkelig sker, finde ud af hvem der får mest gavn, og til sidst hjælpe læger med at vide hvordan man bruger disse stoffer sikkert. Dette validerede spørgeskema er som at få et pålideligt termometer til området.

items.title: Surrender, disidentification, and reappraisal: a qualitative comparison of psilocybin responders and non-responders in treatment-resistant OCD.

summaries.en:
What separates people who find relief from treatment-resistant OCD through psilocybin from those who don't? A new study reveals something striking: responders tend to experience a shift toward surrender and letting go, while non-responders often stay locked in a struggle to control their thoughts. The people who improved managed to separate their sense of self from their OCD, treated themselves with compassion, and spontaneously started seeing their obsessions as trivial rather than threatening—a profound reframing that happens during the experience itself.

Researchers interviewed six people from a clinical trial roughly a month after their single psilocybin dose, comparing those with marked improvement to those with little change. The pattern emerging from these conversations suggests that the magic isn't just chemical—it's deeply psychological. This adds crucial nuance to how we understand psychedelics in mental health: they seem to work best when people can access a state of acceptance rather than resistance. As psychedelic research moves toward real-world treatment, understanding these psychological processes matters enormously.
summaries.da:
Hvad adskiller mennesker, der finder lindring fra behandlingsresistent OCD gennem psykedelika, fra dem, der ikke gør? Et nyt studie afslører noget slående: dem der blev bedre havde tendens til at opleve et skift mod accept og losladen, mens dem der ikke blev bedre ofte blev fastlåst i en kamp for kontrol. De mennesker, der forbedrede sig, lykkedes at adskille deres jeg fra deres OCD, behandlede sig selv med medfølelse, og begyndte spontant at se deres tvangstanker som ubetydelige snarere end truende—en dyb omfortolkning, der sker under oplevelsen selv.

Forskere interviewede seks mennesker fra et klinisk forsøg cirka en måned efter deres enkelt psykedelika-dosis og sammenlignede dem med markant forbedring med dem med minimal ændring. Det mønster, der træder frem fra disse samtaler, foreslår, at magien ikke blot er kemisk—det er dybt psykologisk. Dette tilføjer afgørende nuancer til vores forståelse af psykedelika i mental sundhed: de virker bedst, når mennesker kan få adgang til tilstand af accept snarere end modstand. I takt med at psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig mod behandling i den virkelige verden, betyder det enormt at forstå disse psykologiske processer.

items.title: Exploratory safety, tolerability, and feasibility of psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy for adults with co-occurring treatment-resistant depression and cluster B personality disorders

summaries.en: Here's something remarkable: people with severe depression that hasn't responded to traditional treatments, combined with certain personality patterns, saw their suicidal thoughts cut in half after psilocybin-assisted therapy. In this first-ever trial of its kind, participants showed meaningful improvements that lasted six months—and crucially, the treatment was safe and well-tolerated. Researchers worked with ten adults in a controlled clinical setting, measuring depression symptoms and suicidal ideation carefully before and after the experience. This study opens a door that's been locked until now: it shows psychedelics might help people who've exhausted other options, especially those with complex mental health profiles. As psychedelic research moves beyond 'classic' depression into messier, more complicated cases, this is exactly the kind of careful, honest evidence the field needs to understand who benefits and why.
summaries.da: Her er noget bemærkelsesværdigt: mennesker med alvorlig depression, som ikke reagerer på traditionelle behandlinger, kombineret med visse personlighedsmønstre, oplevede deres selvmordstanker skåret i halvdelen efter psykedelika-assisteret terapi. I dette første forsøg af sin slags så deltagerne meningsfulde forbedringer, der holdt i seks måneder—og afgørende var behandlingen sikker og velkontrolleret. Forskere arbejdede med ti voksne i et kontrolleret klinisk miljø og målte depressionsymptomer og selvmordstanker omhyggeligt før og efter oplevelsen. Dette studie åbner en dør, der har været låst hidtil: det viser, at psykedelika kunne hjælpe mennesker, som har brugt andre muligheder op, især dem med komplekse psykiske sundhedsprofiler. Mens psykedelika-forskning bevæger sig ud over 'klassisk' depression ind i mere indviklede tilfælde, er dette præcis den slags omhyggelig, ærlig evidens, som feltet har brug for for at forstå, hvem der får gavn, og hvorfor.

items.title: Uso de psicodélicos no tratamento da depressão resistente: eficácia clínica e perspectivas terapêuticas

summaries.en: What if one or two carefully guided sessions could lift depression that's resisted years of medication? New research on psychedelics like psilocybin shows rapid antidepressant effects that last weeks or months — a genuinely different approach for people stuck in treatment-resistant depression. Scientists reviewed nine clinical trials from 2016 onwards, finding that psilocybin produced clinically meaningful improvements in depressive symptoms, though results weren't uniformly perfect. Ayahuasca and DMT also showed early promise. This fits into a bigger shift in how we think about mental health: instead of daily pills, we're exploring whether psychedelics in supervised settings could help reset the brain's relationship with mood. The safety data looks encouraging so far, and as more rigorous trials wrap up, we're getting clearer answers about whether this could genuinely transform options for people who've hit dead ends.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis en eller to omhyggeligt vejledt sessionn kunne løfte depression, der har modstået år af medicin? Ny forskning på psykedelika som psilocybin viser hurtige antidepressive effekter, der varer uger eller måneder — en genuint anden tilgang for mennesker, der sidder fast i behandlingsresistent depression. Forskere gennemgik ni kliniske forsøg fra 2016 og fremad og fandt, at psilocybin producerede klinisk meningsfulde forbedringer i depressive symptomer, selvom resultaterne ikke var ensartet perfekte. Ayahuasca og DMT viste også tidlige tegn på virkning. Dette passer ind i en større forskel i, hvordan vi tænker på mental sundhed: i stedet for daglige piller udforsker vi, om psykedelika i overvågede indstillinger kunne hjælpe med at nulstille hjernens forhold til stemning. Sikkerheden ser lovende ud hidtil, og efterhånden som flere stringente forsøg afsluttes, får vi klarere svar på, om dette kunne virkelig transformere muligheder for mennesker, der har ramt dead ends.

items.title: [Intravenous ketamine in suicidal crisis : indications and patient referral].

summaries.en:
When someone's in a suicidal crisis and traditional antidepressants haven't worked, time matters. Intravenous ketamine offers something remarkable: relief in hours, not weeks. It can rapidly reduce suicidal thoughts and psychological distress—a genuine lifeline for people in acute danger. Researchers and clinicians are mapping out exactly when and how to use it, moving beyond the hype to practical guidance.

This study breaks down the real-world pathway: who needs it, how to spot them, and what hospital-based care should look like. As psychedelics and their cousins like ketamine prove they can work fast where conventional treatments have failed, they're reshaping how we think about mental health emergencies. It's not magic—it's careful, specialized medicine that's opening doors for people who desperately need them.
summaries.da:
Når nogen er i selvmordskrise og almindelige antidepressiva ikke har virket, betyder tid noget. Intravenøs ketamin tilbyder noget bemærkelsesværdigt: lindring på timer, ikke uger. Det kan hurtigt reducere selvmordstanker og psykisk lidelse—en reel livline for mennesker i akut fare. Forskere og klinikere kortlægger præcis hvornår og hvordan man bruger det, og går ud over hypen til praktisk vejledning.

Denne undersøgelse tegner vejkortene: hvem har brug for det, hvordan identificerer man dem, og hvordan ser specialiseret hospitalbehandling ud. Når psykedelika og deres slægtninge som ketamin viser, at de virker hurtigt hvor konventionelle behandlinger har fejlet, omformer de vores syn på psykiske sundhedskriser. Det er ikke magi—det er omhyggelig, specialiseret medicin der åbner døre for mennesker der desperat har brug for det.

items.title: Clinical correlates of non-responders to ketamine in terms of self-assessed life engagement among treatment-resistant depression patients.

summaries.en:
Ketamine can lift depression fast—but here's the thing: feeling better symptom-wise doesn't always mean feeling engaged with life again. A new study followed 65 people with treatment-resistant depression who got ketamine and tracked something crucial: whether they could actually enjoy things, get stuff done, and participate in meaningful activities. Half the patients saw real improvements, but half didn't—and researchers discovered some patterns. People whose depression started later in life, those who'd tried ECT before, and those without diabetes were less likely to bounce back to life engagement. Nothing revolutionary yet, but it matters.

Scientists did this by comparing patients who improved versus those who didn't, looking at everything from when their depression began to their life circumstances. What makes this genuinely interesting is that it pushes the conversation beyond just symptom relief. As psychedelics research evolves, we're learning that the real win isn't just feeling less sad—it's recovering the ability to actually live. This study is early, preliminary, but it hints at something researchers are increasingly focused on: understanding why some people respond and others don't, so we can get better at matching people with the right treatment.
summaries.da:
Ketamin kan løfte depression hurtigt—men her er pointen: at føle sig bedre symptommæssigt betyder ikke altid, at man igen føler sig engageret i livet. Et nyt studie fulgte 65 mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression, der fik ketamin, og sporerede noget afgørende: om de faktisk kunne nyde ting, få tingene gjort, og deltage i meningsfulde aktiviteter. Halvdelen af patienterne så rigtig forbedringer, men halvdelen gjorde det ikke—og forskerne opdagede nogle mønstre. Mennesker, hvis depression startede senere i livet, dem der tidligere havde prøvet ECT, og dem uden sukkersyge, havde mindre sandsynlighed for at komme tilbage til livsengagement. Intet revolutionært endnu, men det betyder noget.

Videnskabsmændene gjorde dette ved at sammenligne patienter, der blev bedre versus dem der ikke gjorde, og kiggede på alt fra hvornår deres depression startede til deres livsomstændigheder. Det der gør dette genuint interessant er, at det flytter samtalen ud over blot symptomlindringseffekter. Efterhånden som psykedelika-forskningen udvikler sig, lærer vi, at den rigtige gevinst ikke blot er at føle sig mindre trist—det er at genvinde evnen til faktisk at leve. Dette studie er tidligt, foreløbigt, men det antyder noget, som forskere i stigende grad fokuserer på: at forstå, hvorfor nogle mennesker reagerer og andre ikke gør, så vi kan blive bedre til at matche mennesker med den rigtige behandling.

items.title: Ketamine attenuates habenula activity in response to aversive outcomes during Pavlovian learning.

summaries.en:
Your brain has a tiny but mighty alarm bell called the habenula—and ketamine appears to turn down its volume. In a new study, researchers gave healthy volunteers ketamine or a placebo, then watched their brains learn to expect bad things. The result? Ketamine dulled the habenula's reaction to negative outcomes, potentially helping the brain process difficult experiences without getting stuck in a loop of dread. This matters because depression often involves getting trapped by negative thoughts; if ketamine can quieten that alarm system, it might explain why the drug works so fast.

Scientists used advanced brain imaging on 70 volunteers to map exactly what ketamine does in the human brain—moving beyond animal studies to show the real mechanism at work. This research slots neatly into a bigger puzzle: we're finally starting to understand how psychedelics and ketamine rewire how our brains respond to suffering, opening doors to faster, more targeted treatments for depression and trauma.
summaries.da:
Din hjerne har et lille, men kraftigt alarmklokke kaldet habenula—og ketamin ser ud til at skrue ned for lydstyrken. I et nyt studie gav forskere raske frivillige enten ketamin eller placebo og observerede deres hjerner, mens de lærte at forvente dårlige ting. Resultatet? Ketamin dæmpede habenulas reaktion på negative udfald, hvilket potentielt hjælper hjernen med at behandle svære oplevelser uden at blive fanget i frygt. Dette betyder noget, fordi depression ofte handler om at blive låst fast af negative tanker; hvis ketamin kan stilne det alarmystem, kan det forklare, hvorfor lægemidlet virker så hurtigt.

Forsker brugte avanceret hjerneafbildning på 70 frivillige til at kortlægge præcist, hvad ketamin gør i den menneskelige hjerne—og bevæger sig dermed ud over dyreforsøg til at vise den rigtige mekanisme på arbejde. Denne forskning passer pænt ind i et større puslespil: vi begynder endelig at forstå, hvordan psykedelika og ketamin omkabler, hvordan vores hjerner reagerer på lidelse, og åbner døre til hurtigere, mere målrettede behandlinger for depression og traumer.

items.title: Resetting the hippocampal buffer: a neurocognitive account of psychedelic therapy for anxiety-related psychopathology.

summaries.en: What if the brain's way of getting stuck in anxiety could actually be reset? New research suggests psychedelics might do exactly that by targeting the hippocampus—the brain region that stores and replays worrying memories on repeat. When this system gets overactive, it traps us in loops of fear. The study reveals how psychedelics appear to interrupt this pattern, giving anxiety a chance to break free. Scientists examined how these substances work on the brain's serotonin system to create this shift, looking at both the neuroscience and the psychological experience together. This fits into a larger movement in psychedelic research: moving beyond the question of 'do they work?' toward understanding the precise mechanisms that make healing possible—knowledge that could eventually help us design better treatments for anxiety disorders.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis hjernens måde at blive hængende i angst på faktisk kunne nulstilles? Ny forskning tyder på, at psykedelika kunne gøre præcis det ved at målrette hippocampus—hjernens område, der gemmer og genafspiller bekymrende minder igen og igen. Når dette system bliver overaktivt, fanger det os i frygtloops. Studiet afslører, hvordan psykedelika tilsyneladende afbryder dette mønster og giver angsten en chance for at slippe fri. Forskerne undersøgte, hvordan disse stoffer virker på hjernens serotonin-system for at skabe denne ændring, og så både på neuroviden­skaben og den psykologiske oplevelse sammen. Det passer ind i en større bevægelse inden for psykedelika-forskning: ud over spørgsmålet 'virker de?' mod at forstå de præcise mekanismer, der gør helbredelse mulig—en viden, der eventuelt kunne hjælpe os med at udvikle bedre behandlinger for angstlidelser.

items.title: On the meaning of "plasticity" in neuroscience and mental health research and its relation to the action of psychedelic therapy.

summaries.en:
Scientists are calling out a major confusion in psychedelic research: we've been using the word "plasticity" to mean everything from basic brain flexibility to specific changes we can measure—but these aren't actually the same thing. It's like saying a sponge's ability to be squeezed is the same as it absorbing water. This matters because psychedelic therapy's real power might not come from the brain changes we're currently measuring, and claiming it does risks overselling the science.

A new analysis examined how neuroscientists actually use "plasticity" and found we've been mixing up two completely different concepts, sometimes measuring things that actually lock the brain into fixed patterns rather than opening it up. The researchers aren't saying psychedelics don't work—they're saying we need sharper thinking about *why* they work and what we should actually be measuring. As psychedelic research moves from fringe to mainstream medicine, getting honest about what we really know (and don't know) might be the most important plasticity of all.
summaries.da:
Forskere påpeger en stor forvirring i psykedelika-forskningen: vi har brugt ordet "plasticity" til at betyde alt fra grundlæggende hjernefleksibilitet til specifikke ændringer vi kan måle—men det er faktisk ikke det samme. Det er som at sige, at en svamps evne til at blive klemt er det samme som at opsuge vand. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelika-terapiens virkelige kraft måske ikke kommer fra de hjerneændringer, vi måler i dag, og det risikerer at oversælge videnskaben.

En ny analyse undersøgte, hvordan neuroforskere faktisk bruger ordet "plasticity" og fandt, at vi har blandet to helt forskellige koncepter sammen—nogle gange måler vi ting, der faktisk låser hjernen fast i faste mønstre i stedet for at åbne den op. Forskerne siger ikke, at psykedelika ikke virker—de siger, at vi har brug for skarpere tankegang om *hvorfor* de virker og hvad vi burde måle. Når psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig fra randzone til mainstream medicin, kan ærlig tænkning om, hvad vi virkelig ved (og ikke ved), være den vigtigste plasticity af alt.

items.title: Risks from self-medicating with psychedelic drugs.

summaries.en: People are increasingly turning to psychedelics outside clinical settings to treat depression, anxiety, and trauma—but without professional guidance, the risks can be real. A new study highlights why self-medicating with these powerful substances is risky territory: without proper screening, preparation, and support, people with certain mental health conditions or vulnerabilities could actually be harmed. This research matters because it cuts through the hype. As psychedelics move toward medical legitimacy, we need to be honest about why the controlled, therapeutic setting in clinical trials isn't just bureaucracy—it's protection. Understanding these risks doesn't dampen psychedelic potential; it sharpens our focus on how to harness it safely and responsibly.
summaries.da: Flere mennesker søger selv til psykedelika uden for kliniske rammer for at behandle depression, angst og traumer—men uden professionel vejledning kan risiciene være reelle. Et nyt studie viser, hvorfor selvmedicinering med disse kraftige stoffer er farligt territorium: uden ordentlig screening, forberedelse og støtte kan mennesker med visse psykiske sårbarhedsfaktorer faktisk blive skadet. Denne forskning betyder noget, fordi den gennemhuller myterne. Mens psykedelika bevæger sig mod medicinske godkendelser, er vi nødt til at være ærlige om, hvorfor den kontrollerede, terapeutiske ramme i kliniske forsøg ikke blot er bureaukrati—det er beskyttelse. At forstå disse risici dæmper ikke psykedelikas potentiale; det skærper vores fokus på, hvordan vi kan udnytte det sikkert og ansvarsfuldt.

items.title: No Questions Asked: FDA’s Psychedelics Public Hearing

summaries.en: The FDA just held a public hearing on psychedelics—and the conversation is shifting. For the first time, regulators are seriously engaging with researchers, clinicians, and the public about how to safely develop these medicines. This matters because it signals that psychedelics aren't being dismissed anymore; they're being studied with the same rigor as any other drug. The hearing brought together experts to discuss everything from trial design to patient safety, laying groundwork for how these compounds might move through the approval process. This is where the rubber meets the road: as psychedelic research produces promising results for depression, trauma, and addiction, the real work now is figuring out the regulatory pathway. These conversations between scientists and the FDA are crucial—they're building the bridge between lab discoveries and medicines that could actually help people.
summaries.da: FDA holdt netop en offentlig høring om psykedelika—og samtalen er ved at skifte retning. For første gang tager regulatorer alvorligt fat på at engagere sig med forskere, klinikere og offentligheden om, hvordan man sikkert udvikler disse lægemidler. Det betyder noget, fordi det signalerer, at psykedelika ikke længere bliver afvist; de bliver studeret med samme grundighed som ethvert andet stof. Høringen samlede eksperter for at diskutere alt fra forsøgsdesign til patientsikkerhed og lagde grundlaget for, hvordan disse stoffer kan bevæge sig gennem godkendelsesprocessen. Dette er hvor teorien møder praksis: mens psykedelika-forskning viser lovende resultater for depression, traume og misbrug, handler det rigtige arbejde nu om at finde den regulatoriske vej. Disse samtaler mellem videnskabsfolk og FDA er afgørende—de bygger broen mellem laboratoriediskoverier og lægemidler, der faktisk kunne hjælpe mennesker.
